detail:
NIDDK describes hyperthyroidism, also called overactive thyroid, as a condition in which the thyroid gland makes more thyroid hormones than the body needs. Thyroid hormones affect metabolism, heart rate, and temperature, so excess hormone speeds many body functions up. NIDDK lists causes that can include Graves' disease, an autoimmune condition, overactive thyroid nodules, and inflammation of the thyroid.

Symptoms can include weight loss despite usual eating, rapid or irregular heartbeat, nervousness, tremor, sweating and trouble tolerating heat, frequent bowel movements, fatigue, and sleep problems. Clinicians usually evaluate suspected hyperthyroidism with blood tests for thyroid-stimulating hormone and thyroid hormone levels, and may use additional antibody tests, uptake studies, or imaging to identify the cause, since treatment depends on what is driving the excess hormone.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about hyperthyroidism symptoms and diagnosis.
